terra.problem: Calling the neighbors new and unwelcome adds a timeframe and a feeling the text does not give.
“Even I can tell a fortress from a pile of rubble” risks putting down the baker for choosing that answer.
The text does not say the journey into exile is a long walk or that nobody gets to stay home.
Calling it a “fancy exile” makes light of people being sent into exile.
The traveling-band joke makes light of the exile by imagining a lively trip.
The earlier verses do not say Rabbah will be empty for good, so they cannot be said to be heading toward that outcome.
The verse says if those who do not deserve the cup must drink it; the explanation turns that condition into a completed event.
Hebrews 6:13 gives the reason God swore by Himself to Abraham. The explanation transfers that stated reason to this oath about Bozrah.
The explanation credits pride alone with deceiving Edom, but the verse names both pride and the terror Edom causes.
The verse says passersby will be appalled and scoff; it does not say whether they help.
